Module 01 • Hypothalamus & Pituitary Gland

Hypothalamic-Pituitary Regulation, Anterior Pituitary & ADH Disorders

Endocrine feedback physiology, anterior pituitary tumors & hypopituitarism, and posterior pituitary water balance (DI vs. SIADH) with step-by-step diagnostic trees and exact clinical doses.

Chapter 01

Pituitary Anatomy, Hormones & Master Feedback Rules

Golden Rule

Every endocrine diagnosis answers ONE question via negative feedback: Primary (target gland), Secondary (pituitary), or Tertiary (hypothalamus). Suspected Excess → Suppress it; Suspected Deficiency → Stimulate it!

Anterior EmbryologyRathke Pouch (Oral Ectoderm) • Portal Blood
Posterior EmbryologyNeuroectoderm • SON / PVN Axons
Shared α-SubunitFSH, LH, TSH, hCG (β = Specific!)
Histology MnemonicAcidophils: GPA • Basophils: B-FLAT
Master Endocrine Diagnostic Framework — Excess vs. Deficiency Diagnostic Approach #1
Suspected HORMONE EXCESS
Rule: Autonomous glands fail to suppress.
  • GH Excess: 75g OGTT fails to drop GH
  • Cortisol: 1 mg Overnight Dex fails
  • Aldosterone: IV Saline fails to suppress
Action: Run Suppression Test → Check Trophic!
Suspected DEFICIENCY
Rule: Failed glands cannot respond.
  • Cortisol: 250 mcg Cosyntropin flat
  • ADH (DI): Water Deprivation / Copeptin
  • Pituitary: Check paired target + trophic
Action: Run Stimulation Test → Replace Deficit!
Primary vs. Secondary Decoder
  • Primary Failure: ↓ Target + ↑↑ Trophic
  • Secondary Failure: ↓ Target + ↓/N Trophic
  • Key Neighbors: Superior = Optic Chiasm; Lateral = Cavernous Sinus (CN III, IV, V1/2, VI)
POMC → ACTH + α-MSH (Pigment in Addison!)
Chapter 02

Anterior Pituitary Disorders: Adenomas, Sheehan & Apoplexy

Golden Rule

Prolactinoma is treated MEDICALLY first (even huge macroadenomas with visual loss!). Almost every other symptomatic pituitary adenoma goes to Transsphenoidal Surgery. In hypopituitarism, ALWAYS replace Cortisol BEFORE Levothyroxine!

Diagnostic Approach: Hyperprolactinemia, Acromegaly & Pituitary Mass Diagnostic Approach #2
STEP 1
Exclude Physiologic & Secondary Mimics FIRST: Check Urine β-hCG (Pregnancy) • TSH (↑TRH drives PRL!) • Creatinine • Drug List (Risperidone, Haloperidol, Metoclopramide, Verapamil, SSRIs).
↓
Fasting Prolactin > 200 ng/mL
Diagnosis: Macroprolactinoma (≥10 mm).
  • 25–150 ng/mL: Drugs, stalk effect, or microadenoma (<10 mm).
  • Hook Effect Trap: Huge tumor + falsely mild PRL → Order 1:100 Serum Dilution!
1st-Line: Cabergoline (Medical Shrinkage!)
Suspected Acromegaly (GH)
  • 1. Best Screen: Serum IGF-1 (never random GH — pulsatile!).
  • 2. Confirm: 75g OGTT → GH fails to suppress (>0.4–1 ng/mL).
  • 3. Localize: Pituitary MRI + Mandatory Colonoscopy!
1st-Line: Transsphenoidal Resection
Thunderclap Headache + CN III
Pituitary Apoplexy (EMERGENCY!): Acute bleed into adenoma → visual loss + shock.
  • Sheehan Clue: Postpartum hemorrhage → failure to lactate + amenorrhea.
  • Order Lost: GH → LH/FSH → TSH → ACTH.
STAT IV Hydrocortisone 100 mg + Urgent MRI!
Intern & Exam Prescribing Sheet

Chapter 03

Posterior Pituitary: ADH, Diabetes Insipidus (AVP-D/R) & SIADH

Golden Rule

ADH controls ONE valve: Free Water via Aquaporin-2. Too little ADH = DI (water pours out → ↑Na+). Unregulated ADH = SIADH (water trapped → euvolemic ↓Na+). Guardrail: NEVER correct chronic Na+ faster than 6–8 mEq/L per 24h!

Diagnostic Approach: Polyuria (DI Workup) & Euvolemic Hyponatremia (SIADH) Diagnostic Approach #3
POLYURIA >3 L/d
Check Urine Osmolality: If >300 = Solute diuresis (Glucose/Mannitol/Urea). If <300 mOsm/kg = Water Diuresis → Run Water Deprivation + DDAVP (or Stimulated Copeptin):
↓
Primary Polydipsia
Water Deprivation: Urine concentrates normally (U-Osm > 600).
Baseline Serum Na+: Low-normal.
Tx: Behavioral Fluid Reduction
Central DI (AVP-Deficiency)
Deprivation: Stays dilute (<300).
Post-DDAVP: U-Osm jumps >50%!
Stim. Copeptin: <4.9 pmol/L.
MRI Sella • Tx: Desmopressin
Nephrogenic DI (AVP-Resist.)
Deprivation: Stays dilute (<300).
Post-DDAVP: Minimal change (<10%)!
Causes: Lithium (#1), ↑Ca2+, ↓K+.
Stop Lithium • HCTZ + Amiloride
SIADH CRITERIA
Euvolemic Hypotonic Hyponatremia: Serum Na+ <135 + S-Osm <275 + Inappropriately concentrated U-Osm >100 + U-Na+ >40 + Normal TSH, Cortisol & Kidney function! (Check CXR/CT for Small-Cell Lung Cancer & review SSRIs/Carbamazepine!)
Exact Ward & ICU Prescribing

Chapter 04

Thyroid Physiology, Hypothyroidism & Myxedema Coma

Golden Rule

Master Plate 4.1 once and you know every antithyroid drug mechanism forever. For Levothyroxine: Healthy adults = 1.6 mcg/kg/d; Elderly/CAD = start 12.5–25 mcg; Pregnancy = ↑ dose 25–30% immediately!

#1 Cause (Iodine-Replete)Hashimoto (Anti-TPO >90%, Hürthle cells)
Hashimoto MalignancyPrimary Thyroid MALT Lymphoma
Hidden Lab Clues↓Na+ • ↑LDL • ↑CK • ↑Prolactin
Drug CausesAmiodarone, Lithium, TKIs, PD-1i
Primary (↑TSH, ↓FT4) • Subclinical (↑TSH, N FT4) • Central (↓/N TSH, ↓FT4)

Chapter 05

Hyperthyroidism, Thyroiditis, Thyroid Nodules & Thyroid Cancer

Golden Rule

Separate Over-Synthesis (HIGH RAIU → Methimazole/RAI) from Destructive Thyroiditis (LOW RAIU → NEVER Methimazole!). For every thyroid nodule: TSH + Ultrasound FIRST — only scan if TSH is low!

Diagnostic Approach: Thyrotoxicosis (↓TSH + ↑FT4/T3) — RAIU & TRAb Decoder Diagnostic Approach #4
STEP 1
Low TSH (<0.1) + High Free T4 / Free T3: Check TRAb / TSI antibodies (if clearly Graves eye signs + diffuse goiter = confirmed!). Otherwise run 24-hr I-123 Radioactive Iodine Uptake (RAIU) Scan:
↓
HIGH Diffuse RAIU
Graves Disease (75%)
TRAb/TSI (+), audible bruit, ophthalmopathy, pretibial myxedema.
Methimazole (PTU 1st trim.)
HIGH Patchy / Focal
Toxic MNG (multiple hot areas) OR Toxic Adenoma (1 hot nodule, rest cold).
I-131 Ablation or Surgery
LOW RAIU + ↑Tg
Destructive Thyroiditis:
• Painful + ↑ESR: de Quervain
• Painless + TPO+: Postpartum
• Amiodarone AIT-2
NSAID/Steroid + β-Blocker
LOW RAIU + ↓↓Tg
Factitious Thyrotoxicosis (exogenous Levothyroxine intake!).
Also low RAIU: Struma Ovarii, Iodine load (AIT-1).
Stop Exogenous T4!

Chapter 06

Calcium Homeostasis & Parathyroid Disorders

Golden Rule

Always calculate Corrected Ca = Measured Ca + 0.8 × (4.0 − Albumin) (or ionized Ca) FIRST, then order Intact PTH — it splits every calcium abnormality cleanly in half!

Diagnostic Approach: Hypercalcemia (>10.5 mg/dL) & Hypocalcemia (<8.5 mg/dL) Diagnostic Approach #5
HYPERCALCEMIA
Confirm true ↑ Corrected / Ionized Ca2+ → Measure Intact PTH:
↓
PTH HIGH or Inappropriately Normal
Check 24-hr Urine Ca / Creatinine Clearance Ratio (CCCR):
  • CCCR > 0.02 (Hypercalciuria): Primary Hyperparathyroidism (85% solitary adenoma) or Lithium/Thiazide!
  • CCCR < 0.01 (Hypocalciuria): FHH (CaSR mutation — benign, DO NOT operate!).
Primary HyperPTH → Check Surgical Criteria!
PTH SUPPRESSED (<20 pg/mL) — Non-PTH
  • ↑ PTHrP: Squamous Lung / Renal / Breast CA (#1 inpatient cause!)
  • ↑ 1,25-(OH)2D: Sarcoidosis, TB, Lymphoma
  • SPEP / Free Light Chains: Multiple Myeloma (CRAB!)
  • ↑ 25-(OH)D / Milk-Alkali / Hyperthyroidism
Acute Ca >14: NS 200–300 mL/h + Calcitonin + Zoledronate!
HYPOCALCEMIA
Check Mg2+ & PO4 + PTH: • ↓PTH + ↑PO4 = Hypoparathyroidism (post-thyroidectomy #1, DiGeorge, Mg <1.0!) • ↑PTH + ↓PO4 = Vitamin D Deficiency • ↑PTH + ↑PO4 = CKD or Pseudohypoparathyroidism (GNAS1 / AHO — short 4th/5th metacarpals!)
Primary HyperPTH
Ca2+ ↑PO4 ↓PTH ↑/N
  • "Stones, Bones (osteitis fibrosa cystica), Groans, Psych Overtones" + Short QT.
  • Operate If ANY 1: Ca >1 above ULN, Age <50, T-score ≤−2.5, eGFR <60, or Stones / 24h U-Ca >250–300!
  • Pre-Op Localize ONLY: US + Tc-99m Sestamibi.
Secondary & Tertiary
2°: Ca ↓/N, PTH ↑↑3°: Ca ↑↑, PTH ↑↑↑
  • 2° (CKD #1 / Vit D def): Treat with Sevelamer 800–1600 mg TID + Calcitriol 0.25–0.5 mcg/d + Cinacalcet.
  • 3° (Autonomous post-CKD): Cinacalcet 30–180 mg/d or Subtotal Parathyroidectomy.
HypoPTH Exact Doses
Ca2+ ↓PO4 ↑Chvostek / Trousseau+
  • Acute Tetany / ↑QT: 10% IV Ca Gluconate 1–2 g over 15 min + IV MgSO4 2 g!
  • Chronic: Ca Carbonate 1–3 g/d + Calcitriol 0.25–1 mcg BID (goal Ca 8.0–8.5).
Chapter 07 Essential Added Topic

Metabolic Bone Disease: Osteoporosis, Osteomalacia & Paget Disease

Golden Rule

Decode ANY metabolic bone case in 5 seconds from 4 labs: Osteoporosis = ALL NORMAL; Osteomalacia = ↓Ca, ↓PO4, ↑ALP, ↑PTH; Paget Disease = ISOLATED SKY-HIGH ALP!

Diagnostic Approach: Metabolic Bone Disease Lab Pattern Decoder Diagnostic Approach #6
Osteoporosis (Thin Bone)
Ca NPO4 NALP NPTH N
  • DEXA Screen: Women ≥65 / Men ≥70.
  • Treat If: Fragility fx OR T-score ≤ −2.5 OR Osteopenia + FRAX ≥20% major / ≥3% hip.
1st-Line: Bisphosphonate (Alendronate)
Osteomalacia / Rickets (Soft)
Ca ↓PO4 ↓ALP ↑PTH ↑↑
  • Cause: Severe Vit D def (<10–20 ng/mL), celiac, CKD.
  • X-ray: Looser pseudofractures, diffuse bone pain, proximal weakness.
Vit D3 50,000 IU weekly × 8 wks → 1000–2000/d
Paget Disease (Chaotic Bone)
Ca NPO4 NALP ↑↑↑PTH N
  • Signs: Increasing hat size, CN VIII deafness, bowed tibia, high-output HF; rare osteosarcoma!
  • X-ray: Cotton-wool skull, mosaic histology.
1st-Line: IV Zoledronic Acid 5 mg × 1

Chapter 08

Adrenal Hyperfunction: Cushing Syndrome, Conn Syndrome & CAH

Golden Rule

"GFR = Salt, Sugar, Sex" (the deeper you go, the sweeter it gets). Only Fasciculata & Reticularis depend on ACTH; Glomerulosa (Aldosterone) runs on RAAS & K+ — explaining why Secondary AI never causes hyperkalemia!

Diagnostic Approach: 3-Step Cushing Syndrome Algorithm Diagnostic Approach #7
STEP 1: SCREEN
Exclude Exogenous Steroids (#1 cause!) → Confirm hypercortisolism with ≥2 Positive First-Line Tests: (A) 1 mg Overnight Dex Suppression (8 AM Cortisol >1.8 mcg/dL) • (B) 24-hr Urine Free Cortisol • (C) Late-Night Salivary Cortisol (×2).
↓
STEP 2: ACTH
Measure Morning Plasma ACTH to localize ACTH-Independent vs. ACTH-Dependent disease:
↓
ACTH LOW (<5–10 pg/mL)
ACTH-Independent (Adrenal):
Adrenal adenoma, carcinoma, or bilateral hyperplasia.
Order Adrenal CT → Adrenalectomy
ACTH HIGH + High-Dose Dex SUPPRESSES
Pituitary Cushing Disease (70%):
8 mg Dex suppresses cortisol >50%; CRH stimulates ACTH.
Pituitary MRI (or IPSS) → TSS!
ACTH VERY HIGH + NO Suppression
Ectopic ACTH (SCLC / Carcinoid):
Rapid onset + severe ↓K+ alkalosis + dark pigmentation!
CT Chest/Abdomen → Resect Tumor
Diagnostic Approach: Primary Hyperaldosteronism (Conn Syndrome — 5–10% of HTN!) Diagnostic Approach #8
1. Screen (ARR)PAC / PRA >20–30 + PAC >15 + Low Renin (Safe bridge meds: Verapamil, Hydralazine, Doxazosin!)
→
2. Confirm (Suppress)Oral Salt Load OR IV Saline Infusion → Aldosterone fails to drop!
→
3. Subtype (CT + AVS)Adrenal CT → Adrenal Venous Sampling (AVS) if age >35!
→
4. Exact TreatmentUnilateral: Adrenalectomy
Bilateral: Spironolactone 25–200 mg or Eplerenone 25–50 mg BID

Chapter 09

Adrenal Insufficiency (Addison), Pheochromocytoma & Incidentaloma

Golden Rule

Addison Crisis = catecholamine-refractory shock cured instantly by IV Hydrocortisone 100 mg! Pheochromocytoma = ALWAYS give α-Blocker 10–14 days BEFORE β-Blocker to prevent fatal unopposed α-crisis!

Diagnostic Approach: Adrenal Insufficiency & Adrenal Incidentaloma Workup Diagnostic Approach #9
Adrenal Insufficiency (Cosyntropin Test)
  • 8 AM Cortisol <3 mcg/dL = Confirmed AI; >15–18 = Rules out AI.
  • Indeterminate (3–15): Give 250 mcg Cosyntropin IV/IM → 30/60 min Cortisol <18 mcg/dL confirms AI!
  • ACTH ↑↑ (+ ↓Na/↑K/Bronze): Primary Addison (21-OH Ab / TB).
  • ACTH ↓/N (+ Normal K+): Secondary (Steroid withdrawal #1!).
Crisis: Treat FIRST w/ IV Hydrocortisone 100 mg!
Adrenal Incidentaloma (≥1 cm on CT)
Answer 2 Questions on EVERY Mass:
  • 1. Functional? Order 1 mg Overnight Dex (all) + Plasma Free Metanephrines (all if ≥10 HU!) + ARR (if HTN or ↓K+).
  • 2. Malignant? Unenhanced CT <10 HU & <4 cm = Benign lipid-rich adenoma! >4 cm or >20 HU = High ACC risk → Resect!
NEVER biopsy an adrenal mass before ruling out Pheo!

Chapter 10

Diabetes Mellitus: Diagnosis, Organ-Protective Drugs & Insulin Dosing

Golden Rule

Modern diabetes care = Organ Protection! Pair Metformin with SGLT2i (HF / CKD) or GLP-1 / GIP RA (ASCVD / Obesity). On inpatient wards, calculate Basal-Bolus Insulin (0.4–0.5 U/kg) — NEVER sliding-scale monotherapy!

ADA Diagnostic Criteria (Need 2 Tests Unless Classic Crisis!)
TestNormalPrediabetesDiabetes
HbA1c<5.7%5.7–6.4%≥ 6.5% (Skip in hemolysis/CKD!)
Fasting (8h)<100100–125≥ 126 mg/dL
2-hr 75g OGTT<140140–199≥ 200 mg/dL
Random + Sx——≥ 200 mg/dL (1 test enough!)
Goal A1c <7.0%Frail Elderly <7.5–8%Inpatient 140–180
Diabetes Types — Quick Differentiator
  • Type 1 DM: Autoimmune (Anti-GAD65, IA2, ZnT8+); ↓↓ C-peptide; lifelong insulin.
  • Type 2 DM: Insulin resistance + β-cell decline; obesity, acanthosis nigricans.
  • LADA ("Type 1.5"): Lean adult >30 failing oral meds + GAD65+ → early insulin!
  • MODY (AD, <25 yrs): 3-gen FH, Ab(−). MODY 3 (HNF1A) = low-dose Sulfonylurea; MODY 2 (GCK) = mild, no meds!
Therapeutic Approach: T2DM Organ-Protection Picker & Exact Oral / Injectable Doses Clinical Approach #10
Foundation (ALL T2DM)

• Pioglitazone 15–45 mg (No HF!)
Severe catabolic / A1c >10% → Insulin!
Annual Screening & Exact Organ-Protection Doses
Eye & Kidney Protection
  • Retinopathy: Annual dilated exam (at dx T2DM; 5 yrs T1DM). Proliferative → Anti-VEGF + PRP!
  • Nephropathy: Annual UACR ≥30 mg/g + eGFR → ACEi/ARB (Lisinopril 10–40 mg) + SGLT2i + Finerenone 10–20 mg/d!
Neuropathy & Foot
  • Screen: Annual 10-g Monofilament exam.
  • Pain 1st-Line: Duloxetine 60 mg/d or Pregabalin 75–150 mg BID or Gabapentin.
  • Ulcer: Offload + probe-to-bone (osteomyelitis!) + ABI.
CV Risk & Gestational DM
  • CV (#1 Death): BP <130/80 + Statin for ALL T2DM aged 40–75!
  • GDM: Screen at 24–28 wks. 1st-Line Med = INSULIN (goals: fast <95, 1h <140, 2h <120). Postpartum 75g OGTT at 4–12 wks!
Chapter 11 Essential Added Topics

Non-Diabetic Hypoglycemia (Insulinoma) & Dyslipidemia / Statins

Golden Rule

Confirm Whipple Triad (Symptoms + Glucose <55 + Relief with carbs) FIRST, then decode the 72-Hour Supervised Fast using just 3 labs: Insulin, C-Peptide, and Sulfonylurea Screen!

Diagnostic Approach: Non-Diabetic Hypoglycemia — 72-Hour Fast Lab Decoder Diagnostic Approach #11
EtiologyPlasma InsulinC-PeptideProinsulinSulfonylurea ScreenNext Action
Insulinoma (10% MEN 1!) ↑ (≥3 μU/mL) ↑ (≥0.6) ↑↑ Negative CT/MRI/EUS Pancreas → Enucleation (Pre-op: Diazoxide)
Sulfonylurea Surreptitious ↑ ↑ ↑ POSITIVE! Admit 24–48h + Octreotide 50–100 mcg SC q6–8h!
Exogenous Insulin ↑↑↑ ↓↓ SUPPRESSED ↓ Negative Factitious / Medication error! (Synthetic insulin has NO C-peptide!)
Non-Islet Tumor (IGF-2) / Liver ↓ ↓ ↓ Negative Check IGF-2:IGF-1 ratio, Cortisol (Addison), LFTs, Alcohol!
Acute Hypoglycemia Emergency Doses
  • Awake ("Rule of 15"): 15–20 g oral fast carbs → recheck CBG in 15 min!
  • Unconscious + IV: D50W 25–50 mL IV push (or D10W 100–250 mL).
  • No IV Access: Glucagon 1 mg IM/SC or 3 mg Intranasal.
  • Alcoholic / Malnourished: Give IV Thiamine 100 mg BEFORE/WITH Dextrose!
Dyslipidemia & High-Intensity Statins
  • 4 Statin Groups: (1) Clinical ASCVD, (2) LDL ≥190 (FH!), (3) DM 40–75 yrs, (4) 10-yr ASCVD ≥20%.
  • High-Intensity (≥50% ↓LDL): Atorvastatin 40–80 mg or Rosuvastatin 20–40 mg.
  • Add-Ons (LDL Goal <55–70): Ezetimibe 10 mg/d → Evolocumab 140 mg SC q2wk.
  • TG >500–1000 (Pancreatitis!): Fenofibrate 145 mg/d + Icosapent Ethyl 2 g BID!

Chapter 12

Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) & Female Gonadal Disorders

Golden Rule

PCOS is a diagnosis of exclusion — rule out the 4 mimics first (β-hCG, TSH, Prolactin, 8 AM 17-OHP for NC-CAH!), then treat strictly around ONE question: Does she want pregnancy now or not?

Diagnostic Approach: Secondary Amenorrhea & PCOS Mimic Exclusion Stepper Diagnostic Approach #12
STEP 1
Rule Out Pregnancy FIRST (Urine/Serum β-hCG) → Then order 4 baseline labs: TSH + Prolactin + FSH/LH + 8 AM 17-OH Progesterone (<200 rules out Non-Classic CAH!) + Total/Free Testosterone.

Pelvic US + Adrenal CT STAT!
FSH HIGH (>25–40 ×2)
Premature Ovarian Insufficiency (<40 yrs): check Karyotype, FMR1, 21-OH Ab.
HRT until Age 51 (Bone/CV)!
FSH / LH LOW
Hypothalamic Amenorrhea (stress, low BMI, athletes) or Pituitary tumor!
Weight/Calorie Restore / MRI

Confirmed PCOS! Mandatory 2-hr 75g OGTT + Lipids + Endometrial protection!
COCs OR Letrozole (Fertility)

Chapter 13

Male Gonadal Disorders, Gynecomastia & Pubertal Disorders

Golden Rule

Always confirm TWO fasting 8 AM Total Testosterone levels (<264–300 ng/dL) before diagnosing male hypogonadism — then let LH & FSH split Primary (Testes) from Secondary (Pituitary)!

Diagnostic Approach: Male Hypogonadism — 8 AM Testosterone → LH / FSH Fork Visual Decision Tree
STEP 1
Confirm Low Fasting 8 AM Total Testosterone (×2 separate mornings) (Check Free T if obese/low SHBG) → Measure LH & FSH:
↓
LH & FSH HIGH — Primary (Hypergonadotropic)
  • Klinefelter Syndrome (47,XXY — #1 genetic!): Tall eunuchoid, small firm testes (<4 mL), gynecomastia, azoospermia!
  • Other: Mumps orchitis, chemo/radiation, cryptorchidism.
Order Karyotype • Tx: Testosterone Replacement
LH & FSH LOW/NORMAL — Secondary (Hypogonadotropic)
  • Check Prolactin, Iron/Ferritin (Hemochromatosis), & Pituitary MRI!
  • Kallmann Syndrome: Failed GnRH neuron migration → Hypogonadism + ANOSMIA!
  • Reversible: Opioids, anabolic steroids, severe obesity.
Want Fertility? Use hCG/FSH — NEVER Exogenous T!
Gynecomastia (↑ Estrogen : Testosterone Ratio)
  • Exam: Rubbery concentric subareolar disc (>2 cm) — exclude soft fat (pseudo) & hard eccentric male breast CA!
  • Classic Drugs ("DISCO"): Digoxin, Isoniazid, Spironolactone, Cimetidine/Ketoconazole/Finasteride, Opioids/Alcohol/Marijuana.
  • Workup: β-hCG, LH, T, E2, TSH, PRL, LFTs (rule out Testicular Germ-Cell/Leydig tumor!).
  • Tx: Stop drug; painful <1 yr → Tamoxifen 10–20 mg/d × 3–6 mo.
Pubertal Disorders & Testosterone Traps
  • Precocious (<8 F / <9 M): Central (↑LH/FSH): MUST do Brain MRI in boys → Tx: continuous Leuprolide! Peripheral (↓LH/FSH): CAH, McCune-Albright.
  • Delayed (>13 F / >14 M): #1 = Constitutional Delay (delayed bone age → reassure!).
  • Testosterone Tx Doses: T-Cypionate 50–100 mg IM/SC weekly or 1.62% gel. Monitor Hct (<54%) & PSA! Avoid in prostate CA or desired fertility (suppresses sperm!).

Chapter 14

MEN Syndromes, Neuroendocrine Tumors & Miscellaneous Endocrinology

Golden Rule

Tumors in ≥2 endocrine glands or young-onset presentation → think Autosomal Dominant MEN! Memorize Plate 14.1 and NEVER forget: Screen & α-block Pheochromocytoma BEFORE touching the thyroid!

High-Yield Miscellaneous Endocrine Syndromes & Obesity Pharmacotherapy
Carcinoid Syndrome & GEP-NETs
  • Rule: Midgut serotonin NET causes syndrome ONLY after liver mets (bypassing hepatic breakdown) or bronchial primary.
  • Triad: Episodic flushing + watery diarrhea/wheezing + Right-sided valvular fibrosis (TR/PS) + Pellagra (B3)!
  • Dx & Tx: 24-hr Urine 5-HIAA + Ga-68 DOTATATE PET → Octreotide LAR 20–30 mg IM q4wk (acute crisis: 50–100 mcg SC/IV!).
Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndromes
  • APS-1 (AR • AIRE): Childhood triad: Candidiasis + HypoPTH + Addison ("Candida-Para-Addison").
  • APS-2 (Schmidt • HLA-DR3/4): Adult females: Addison + Thyroid (Hashimoto/Graves) + Type 1 DM!
  • Ward Pearl: T1DM suddenly having unexplained hypoglycemia → Screen for Addison & Hypothyroidism!
Paraneoplastic & Checkpoint Inhibitors
  • SIADH & Ectopic ACTH: Small-Cell Lung Cancer (SCLC).
  • Humoral ↑Ca2+ (↑PTHrP): Squamous Lung, Renal, Breast CA.
  • Ectopic 1,25-Vit D: Hodgkin / Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma.
  • Checkpoint Inhibitors (Nivo/Pembro/Ipi): Hypophysitis (↓ACTH!), Thyroiditis, Fulminant T1DM (DKA!), Adrenalitis!
Modern Obesity Medications (Exact Doses)
  • Indications: BMI ≥30 OR BMI ≥27 + comorbidity.
  • Tirzepatide (~20–22% wt loss!): 2.5 mg SC/wk → up to 15 mg/wk (titrate q4wk).
  • Semaglutide (~15% + CV benefit!): 0.25 mg SC/wk → 2.4 mg/wk.
  • Bariatric Surgery: BMI ≥40 (or ≥35 w/ comorb) → lifelong Iron, B12, Folate, Ca, Vit D!
Chapter 15

Life-Threatening Endocrine Emergencies — ER / ICU Rapid-Action Guide

Golden Rule

In endocrine emergencies, DRUG SEQUENCE SAVES LIVES — giving the right drug in the wrong order can be fatal! Master Plate 15.1 (DKA/HHS) and the 6-Emergency Rapid-Action Matrix below cold!

Master ER / ICU Rapid-Action Matrix — Exact Golden-Hour Sequences & Fatal Traps
1. Thyroid Storm (Burch-Wartofsky ≥45)"5 P's Order!"
  1. Propranolol: 60–80 mg PO q4–6h (or Esmolol IV drip) — blocks HR & T4→T3!
  2. PTU FIRST: 500–1000 mg load → 250 mg q4h (blocks synthesis + T4→T3!).
  3. Iodine (1 HR LATER!): SSKI 5 drops q6h or Lugol's 10 drops q8h (Wolff-Chaikoff!).
  4. Hydrocortisone: 100 mg IV q8h + Acetaminophen cooling.
FATAL TRAP: NEVER give Iodine before PTU! NEVER give Aspirin (displaces T4 from TBG)!
2. Myxedema Coma (30–50% Mortality)Steroid FIRST!
  1. Airway + Hydrocortisone FIRST: 100 mg IV q8h (rules out adrenal crisis!).
  2. IV Levothyroxine: 200–400 mcg slow IV → 50–100 mcg IV daily (± T3 if refractory).
  3. Support: Passive rewarming (blankets), treat infection, watch ↓Na+ & ↑CO2!
FATAL TRAP: NEVER give LT4 without IV Hydrocortisone! NO active warming (vasodilatory shock)!
3. Acute Adrenal CrisisShock + ↓Na + ↑K
  1. IV Hydrocortisone STAT: 100 mg IV bolus → 50 mg IV q6h (covers mineralocorticoid too!).
  2. Rapid Fluids: 0.9% NS 1–2 L IV rapid + D5W if hypoglycemic!
  3. Treat Trigger: Sepsis, trauma, surgery, or abrupt steroid cessation.
FATAL TRAP: NEVER delay IV Hydrocortisone waiting for Cortisol/Cosyntropin lab results!
4. Pheochromocytoma Crisisα BEFORE β!
  1. IV α-Blocker FIRST: IV Phentolamine 5 mg bolus (q2–5 min) OR IV Nicardipine / Clevidipine.
  2. ONLY After α-Control: Add short-acting IV Esmolol for severe tachyarrhythmia.
  3. Transition: Oral Phenoxybenzamine/Doxazosin + salt/fluids 10–14d pre-op.
FATAL TRAP: Giving a β-blocker alone triggers catastrophic unopposed α-vasoconstriction!
5. Acute Severe HypocalcemiaTetany / ↑QT
  1. IV Calcium Gluconate: 10% 1–2 g in 50 mL D5W over 10–20 min on telemetry!
  2. Continuous Drip (if refractory): 10 g Ca Gluconate in 1 L D5W at 50 mL/hr.
  3. Replete Magnesium: IV MgSO4 2 g (low Mg2+ blocks PTH release!).
FATAL TRAP: Refractory hypocalcemia will NOT correct until severe hypomagnesemia is repleted!
6. DKA / HHS Critical PitfallsWard ICU Alerts
  1. Euglycemic DKA (SGLT2i): Glucose 140–200 + pH <7.3 + ketones → IV Insulin + D5W!
  2. Anion Gap Closure: Never stop IV insulin based on glucose — wait for AG ≤12 & HCO3 ≥18 + 2-hr SC overlap!
  3. Pediatric Cerebral Edema: Sudden headache/bradycardia → IV Mannitol 0.5–1 g/kg (or 3% saline).
FATAL TRAP: Starting IV Insulin when K+ <3.3 mEq/L causes lethal hypokalemic arrest!
